notes.title: 7/24 - Project Update
notes.content:
Hello! I know there has been a lack of updates for about a month or two.
The project is just not moving that much as we prepare for the demo launch.

The open signups for the playtest is closed. Everyone who has access, is still in, please continue to help! It's very much appreciated.

Moving forward, we plan to drop the demo proper on August 5th. This playtest is the same as the demo and although reflects the game, these levels will not be in the game as they are. This is pretty much a vertical slice/tech demo... not so much a "beta" if that makes sense.

I want to take a few steps back and start clean with the project and game building. Especially as the narrative continues to be written and re-written, starting clean with production is going to make a lot more sense. Especially from an optimization point of view. Steam Deck is playable but kind of crap to be honest, anything under 60 fps is unacceptable. So this is probably the biggest reason of them all.

The demo will be "Windows Only" ... so no steam deck.... but the playtest will continue to allow for it. I don't want the players to have a bad initial experience.

The main theme/opening track to our OST has been worked on and we are preparing to announce it to the world too, you can get a preview here:

[previewyoutube=v_Nu38g2MYw;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Again, we welcome feedback. We're very dependent on the players to tell us what works as we are about as small of a developer as can be with little resource. We read and try to respond to everything!

Thanks so much, I'm at comic-con this week trying to find more help to make this thing better....
we're still pretty far from having a game but I think the play test is a good "demo" of what it will be. And I hope it's fun!

One more thing, for those of you in San Diego, we will be showing the game at UCSD on the 29th at Atkins Hall from 5:30PM to 9PM. Come talk to me or send your friends! Thanks - Brandon

notes.title: 6/27 - Locked Chapel Back Door
notes.content:
One of the biggest sources of complaint is when players ignore the Main quest line directions and go straight out the back door believing that is normal progression, when it is meant to be quite difficult and for Vivi to be higher level. Once you know the controls, it's fine, but in the first 2 mins you will not.
So that area is gated by the same yellow key that gates progression to the East part of the chapel as well. Very small design change.

Also, this isn't really meant to be the "start" of the game, so much as a technical demo so that you can touch a large number of mechanics and understand what is capable of the game...it is supposed to feel like a "vertical slice", perhaps of mid-game but also easy enough so it doesn't punish 'new users'.

It's a weird balance, and this is a DEMO.... I think we are still scheduled to go live around 7/22. I need to have the new name and store page up much earlier. I will be closing *signups* for the playtest, but do stick around if you feel inclined. Thanks!

There is a lot of great design suggestions in the feedback. I need to comb through and prioritize/schedule them in.

I need to take more time with BizDev related things as well.

Thanks for playtesting! I think the build is pretty solid... it will get better. It will get battle tested. Then a demo will finally drop.

notes.title: 4/23 -- Playtest Results
notes.content:
Our score actually dropped a bit, but the median went up.
In general, the game is not ready yet. The demo is delayed. 
NextFest is a definite NO.

We don't really have money. We can't get exposure without a demo. The demo has to be built without money.... It's another month of living really tight.

I *[b]downgraded the graphics[/b]*, hopefully this allows for Steam Deck's revival. The 'graphics' are not as important as the gameplay, illustrations, and sound to me. This is a truth for the genre.

I'm tempted to release like HD builds with all the ray tracing enabled as an option... or the opposite release a faster low graphics version for much less money or something. I just dont think theres any platform that would allow for that.

So the game is going to be in flux, we are out of playtest. The next one, let's aim for in 2 weeks? The schedule is "relaxed". We're going to get it right. We're going to fix what ails y'all and make better what you love.

Also in this build is a 1 double jump limit. (most requested change!)
Someone really loved jump spamming (as do I!)  but I nerfed it.
There will be equipment to let you have it back in the future.

-Brandon

notes.title: 4/6 - megaquest under the knife!

There are 3 areas, I think it would be pretty straight forward for a quest giver to give you a hammer and hints as to where these locations are on the map, if you recover the notes or artifacts found there and return to him you will get a reward + xp... this can go alongside whatever main quest line leads you to the boss room which also really needs a ton of work. so i think maybe ill just try to bug fix, polish, and get more of what i mentioned complete. then we will be ready to see the doc. well we wont be ready, but we need to find out what we need to get done before we go live with a demo! the target for that is mid may, to get vetted for nextfest. which is mid-june. so timing is good, hopefully its not more than a month of work in the diagnosis!

notes.title: Quest tracking!
notes.content:
A barebones quest interface for quest data is now in the pause menu.

The quest entries do track and will check off as you collect lore items or do things in the world.
It is just to get the ball rolling, i think the system doesnt need to do too much but it will be nice to have a complete get quest do quest get reward loop in place. it can also drive the main story line if needed. 

right now there are 3 fake quests in the ui just so it can navigate a bit, the lore items for the first quest is available so that will work.

we are pretty much "feature complete"... but not really because not all the features are complete, but they are all in the game in a minimal state.

given what is in the game now, realistically the level should be re-thought out a bit... maybe there just needs to be more real estate to demonstrate all the things we need to show too...
its time to build, more seriously, more narratively driven, more intentionally... and yes i will scrap or make the boss fight better, that is actually probably a year old and one of the first bits of the game that needs to be re-done.

also on a completeness point of view, there will be less loose ends. and more content. more illustrations. more sound. its going to be a fuller experience and that can help the games first impressions.

If we can execute on those items, i think we can raise our score up into the 7/8 range before NextFest. With the goal of having the demo to further massage out available a month before (May) NextFest in (June) 

This is all achievable, if it works out well maybe we can have a real nice comic-con (July) this year!

It's also nice to know that from concept to in-game, we can get new spells in Very fast! Being able to make lots of content hopefully will be a strength of this indie game...

notes.title: 3/29 major change to room spawning.
notes.content:
health is restored to previous damage state after leaving the room if the npc is not killed.
if the npc is killed, then respawns are based on last spawn time (room entry) before death.
which is set at 2 minutes.

its probably not important how thats all set up. but that its less annoying to backtrack.
people were concerned about farming and were upset at losing progress unintendedly.

its now a thing. spawn cooldowns and restored damage.

the upwards dagger attack was shortened in time as well.

these changes are in response to overwhelming feedback of hating the room spawners as they were but understanding the old school design approach. i think this is a fair modernization of the mechanic.

enjoy!

notes.title: 3/29 more adjustments, bug fixes, notes.
notes.content:
- vivi is about 10% faster than previously
- jump physics adjustments, added 10% to jump height 15% to double jump height. gravity is applied on jump, previously was removed. originally had it.
- naming in the options menu for graphics are now set to standard names rather than numbers which was confusing when low numbers meant better gfx etc...

- It is recommended to not use FXAA as the anti-alias but it is the default. I think TSR looks best over here.(this is probably the biggest source of the blurriness)

- I think the majority of the issues are also with nvidia cards which i do not have a machine i can test with at the moment. this probably requires tuning, dlss is better for it for sure. it will probably be in for the next round of play testing.

notes.title: 3/22 - Post GDC Patch Notes

We are back at it! (By we I mean Me, but including you!)

GDC was a great learning opportunity, and just like the last show I hope MQ becomes twice as awesome as a result. Immediate Roadmap:

New weapons are in the pipe, and I am going to redesign some of the lock and keys to be a bit more localized. (ie. players assume the red key is close to red lock).
The game begins a bit differently, there will be an optional tutorial level added as well.
Narrative lines have not been updated to reflect the story changes yet. They will be shortly.
More lines for the NPCs and Quests are coming soon.
More polish is needed, VFX and SFX/music will get some much needed attention.
Game/Level Design will undergo much more attention from a narrative lens.

THANK YOU TO EVERYONE I MET AT GDC! 

I am beyond exhausted and am continuing to recover, but the work has been cut out... and we are going to shape this game into something better, then repeat, until we have a great game. That's just how it goes. Thanks for playtesting, ETA for Demo release is May 1st.

notes.title: 1/10 Large Change to STA system
notes.content:
After reflecting on playtests I think the stamina system should be more discrete.

It now behaves a bit more inspired by Ori... and there is a new temporary meter at the bottom of the screen. The old meter is still in there but will go next build...

+ the user always can keep a mental count of stamina bars left now that its discrete
units of 1 are easier than "30" which i watched someone literally count down. this simplifies the mental math by at least one divide... the visual is simplified too.

+/- the system is slower, you have to wait a full unit to get to consume it... this makes me less happy now that ive had continuous... but i think a buff of like 2x regen rate would feel better. and once you have enough you wont really feel limited by it. unless we want to charge more for special moves... 

+ some other things, doors now only open inward. most pickups have a vfx attached to them to make them stand out even more.

- the spanish translation i think sucks. i dont know for sure because im not a speaker... but i can see the inconsistency in terms... i might have this professionally done closer to the demo release. 

+ another big change i want to implement is spawn ins and a small window for it. this way there are less surprises entering a room. this might be difficult to do across all npcs, ill probably have to touch as many as all of them... so we might just live with this complaint... which i take very seriously because it is indeed unfair to be dropped into battle. maybe its taggable for difficulty because its not entirely unreasonable to have the defenders have the upper hand... its just. not. fun. imho.

- i'm behind on polish and design because i wanted to fix other features... the demo probably will get pushed back hopefully not out of nextfest range... i might save nextfest for june and just still have the demo out around the same time if i cant get it polished up...

notes.title: 1/3 - Fast Travel with Gates and Portals!!!
notes.content:
Okay, the new spells are in. You can move through the world via teleportation, because that's how you move when you can use magic!

Gate -- returns you to the starting city. There will be more gates... when there are more cities.

Portals -- are activatable sites that you will pass through exploring a map. If you activate one you can use it to teleport to via a Port spell. The port spell chooses the closest activated portal, so its kind of like bread crumbs, if you want to leap back far and fast you will consume all the bread crumbs you left behind, but if you walk a little towards the next you can keep more active and traverse quicker that way. It would be easy enough to make a more traditional go anywhere system, but I like how this fits into the world. So try it out, let me know your thoughts! :)

Some updated animations went in recently, I need to return to building and polishing for demonstration purposes still; I just thought these few features were critical to have in the slice.

Thanks for playtesting!!!

More soon! We're flying! Or faster than that, we're tele-porting!

-Brandon

notes.title: Update 10/6/24 - B
notes.content:
I am testing the ogre's being somewhat "evasive".

There is now a chance for them to jump back or roll forward before attacking, along with just attacking. This is to guess if you jump back or slide forward as well. It is a bit of rock paper scissors, but the player still has plenty of window to have the upper hand.

I am receiving a lot of feedback about the enemies being too easy, too predictable. It is a rule that making a "smarter ai" is not usually more fun. It needs to be entertaining is the top goal. On the other hand I am receiving feedback that enemies are a bit too hard and difficult to react to as well.

So this is a bit of a test to see if its more well received. It is still certainly easy to avoid for me... But every once in awhile it gets me :) and maybe that's enough... it is also the game's introduction, and i think the expectation of easy to smash needs to be met as well.

Some of these ideas will carry forward with other human-like enemies too and it will be interesting to see if its something that can be dialed up a bit.
